intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Sunset Sailing & Snorkeling Around Santorini Caldera
experiences.description: Join a small-group catamaran cruise departing in the late afternoon around the volcanic caldera of Santorini. Snorkel in crystal-clear Aegean waters, visit the Red and White beaches, and enjoy a traditional Greek mezze spread with local wine on board as you watch the legendary Oia sunset from the sea.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora)
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local food guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and shop for local spices and ingredients. This indoor-friendly tour is perfect for avoiding midday heat.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Morning Visit
experiences.description: Arrive early at the stunning Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete to enjoy its famous pink-tinged sand and shallow turquoise lagoons before the midday crowds and heat arrive. Wade across the shallow sandbar to the small island, collect sea glass, and swim in calm, warm waters. Pack a local picnic from a nearby bakery for a perfect morning escape.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in a Cretan Village
experiences.description: Spend a morning in a family-run kitchen in a traditional Cretan village learning to prepare authentic dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and galaktoboureko (custard pastry). The class takes place indoors making it an ideal midday heat or rain alternative. Enjoy the meal you prepare with local raki and wine.

experiences.name: Evening Taverna Crawl in Nafplio Old Town
experiences.description: As temperatures cool in the evening, stroll through the charming Venetian old town of Nafplio and hop between traditional tavernas sampling local Peloponnesian specialties: grilled octopus, tomatokeftedes, fresh grilled fish, and local Nemea red wine. The cobblestone streets and neoclassical architecture create a magical atmosphere perfect for a leisurely evening of authentic Greek dining and culture.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Admire the illuminated Acropolis from street level. Grab a cheap souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk to fuel your first night.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a snack at the airport — a tyropita (cheese pie) from a bakery kiosk for around €2
meals.dinner: Street souvlaki wrap (pita gyros) near Monastiraki Square — budget €3–5 per wrap

day_by_day.notes: Buy an Ath.ena reloadable transit card at the airport Metro station for cheaper bus and metro fares throughout your Athens stay. Keep €10–15 cash handy for first-day transport and snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket costs around €20 and covers multiple archaeological sites — great value. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Ancient Agora of Athens (covered by the combined ticket). Explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, wander through the Monastiraki flea market for free browsing and local color.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Thisio neighborhood for sunset views of the Acropolis from the pedestrian promenade. Enjoy an affordable dinner at a local taverna on the side streets.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri (sesame bread ring) and a freddo espresso from a street vendor — under €3 total
meals.lunch: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and a cold drink from a local bakery near the Agora — around €4
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Thisio — try moussaka or pastitsio with a small carafe of house wine — budget €10–13 per person

day_by_day.notes: The combined Acropolis ticket (€20 in peak season) covers the Acropolis, Ancient Agora, Roman Agora, Kerameikos, and more — use it across multiple days. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the National Archaeological Museum (one of the world's great museums) — entry around €10. Marvel at the Antikythera Mechanism, Mycenaean gold artifacts, and ancient sculptures. Spend 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the colorful Varvakios Central Market (Athens Central Market) — a free and vibrant experience. See the fish, meat, and spice stalls. Browse the surrounding streets for cheap olives, honey, and local produce. Pick up budget picnic supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a picnic dinner on Filopappou Hill with panoramic views of the Acropolis and the city at dusk. Alternatively, find a cheap eatery in the Exarchia neighborhood, known for affordable, authentic food.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast if included, or a Greek yogurt with honey from a nearby café — €3–4
meals.lunch: Picnic from the Central Market — olives, feta, bread, tomatoes — around €5–6 total
meals.dinner: Exarchia neighborhood taverna — hearty Greek salad, grilled chicken, and bread — €8–11 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Central Market is closed on Sundays, so today (Thursday) is perfect. Exarchia is a bohemian, student-friendly area with some of Athens' most affordable and authentic restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro Line 1 to Piraeus port (around €1.50). Board an early ferry to the island of Aegina — ferries run frequently and cost around €8–12 one way. Arrive in about 40 minutes. Walk or rent a cheap bicycle to explore the charming port town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Temple of Aphaia (bus or taxi from port, ~€3 each way) — one of Greece's best-preserved ancient temples with sea views. Afterward, head to one of Aegina's quiet beaches like Agia Marina for a swim in the clear Aegean water.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Piraeus (check last ferry times — usually around 9:00–10:00 PM). Grab dinner at the port before heading back to Athens.

meals.breakfast: Eat before leaving Athens — a tiropita or spanakopita from a bakery near the hostel — €2–3
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or calamari at a simple waterfront taverna in Aegina port — budget €10–13
meals.dinner: Souvlaki or gyros wrap near Piraeus port before catching the metro back — €4–5

day_by_day.notes: Aegina is famous for its pistachios — buy a small bag as a snack or souvenir for €3–5. Check ferry schedules at the port or online (e.g., openseas.gr) the night before. This is a fantastic budget day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early KTEL bus or train from Athens to Nafplio (approximately 2–2.5 hours, around €13–15). Nafplio is one of Greece's most beautiful small towns. Check into a budget guesthouse and drop your bags.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nafplio's charming old town on foot — it's compact and walkable. Visit the Palamidi Fortress (climb 999 steps or take a taxi up for €5) for sweeping views over the Argolic Gulf. Stroll along the waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the neoclassical streets of the old town. Browse the small shops and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere. Have dinner at a local taverna tucked into the backstreets.

meals.breakfast: Quick bite at Athens bus station — a cheese pie and coffee — €3–4
meals.lunch: Souvlaki or a simple mezze plate at a café in Nafplio old town — €7–9
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna dinner in Nafplio — try lamb chops (paidakia) or stuffed peppers — €11–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: KTEL buses depart from Athens' Kifissos Bus Terminal (Terminal A) — take bus X93 from the airport or a city bus from central Athens. Nafplio is a great base for exploring the Peloponnese on a budget.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or join a cheap shared taxi to Epidaurus (about 30 km from Nafplio, ~€3–5 each way). Visit the ancient Theatre of Epidaurus — one of the best-preserved ancient theatres in the world. Entry around €12. Test the famous acoustics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and spend the afternoon at Arvanitia Beach — a small, free pebble beach just a 10-minute walk from the old town. Swim in the crystal-clear water and relax in the afternoon sun (average high 23°C — perfect beach weather).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset from the Acronauplia castle walls (free to walk up). Have a leisurely dinner near the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts at a café in Nafplio — €4–5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or a gyros wrap from a local snack bar near Epidaurus — €4–5
meals.dinner: Waterfront taverna in Nafplio — fresh grilled sea bream (tsipoura) with salad and bread — €12–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: June 21 is the summer solstice — the longest day of the year. Enjoy the extended daylight for extra beach and sightseeing time. Arvanitia Beach has free access and a small café nearby.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a KTEL bus from Nafplio toward Athens, then connect to a ferry or direct bus to Santorini. Alternatively, travel to Piraeus and take an overnight ferry to Santorini (around €35–50 in a deck/economy seat). If budget allows, a direct ferry from Piraeus takes about 5–8 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the afternoon/evening ferry from Piraeus to Santorini. Relax on deck and enjoy the Aegean scenery. Pack snacks and water to save money on ferry food.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Santorini (Athinios port) late evening or overnight. Take the local bus (€1.80) to Fira or your accommodation area. Check into a budget hostel or studio in Fira or Perissa.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Nafplio guesthouse or a local bakery — €3–5
meals.lunch: Packed picnic on the ferry — bread, cheese, olives, fruit bought from a Nafplio market — €5–6
meals.dinner: Simple meal at a budget taverna in Fira upon arrival, or eat on the ferry — €8–10

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance via ferryscanner.com or openseas.gr to get the best budget prices. Deck/economy class is the cheapest option. The overnight ferry saves on one night's accommodation cost.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Fira (the island's capital) on foot — walk the caldera-edge path and enjoy the dramatic volcanic views. Visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera (entry ~€6) to learn about the Minoan civilization buried by the volcanic eruption.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the local bus (€1.80) to Perissa or Perivolos — Santorini's famous black sand beaches on the south coast. Spend the afternoon swimming and sunbathing. Beach access is free; rent a sunbed for €5–8 if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Santorini sunset from Imerovigli (a quieter, less crowded alternative to Oia) — walk the caldera path from Fira. Return to Fira for a budget dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or a bakery in Fira — fresh bread, cheese, and coffee — €4–5
meals.lunch: Gyros or souvlaki wrap from a snack bar near Perissa beach — €4–5
meals.dinner: Budget taverna in Fira — try fava (yellow split pea dip), tomato keftedes (Santorini specialty), and grilled meat — €10–13 per person

day_by_day.notes: Santorini is generally expensive, but you can keep costs down by eating at local tavernas away from the caldera edge, using public buses instead of taxis, and buying groceries from the local supermarket for snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the famous Fira-to-Oia caldera trail (approximately 10 km, 3–4 hours) — completely free and one of the most spectacular walks in Greece. The path offers breathtaking views of the caldera, volcanic islands, and whitewashed villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Oia and explore the iconic blue-domed churches and narrow alleyways. Browse the local shops (window shopping is free!). Visit the Oia Castle ruins for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Oia for the world-famous sunset (crowds gather at the castle — arrive early for a good spot). Take the local bus back to Fira (€1.80) after sunset. Have a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the hike — Greek yogurt, honey, and a coffee — €4–5
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for the hike — bread, feta, tomatoes, and water from a Fira supermarket — €5–6
meals.dinner: Taverna in Fira — dakos (Cretan rusk salad), grilled octopus, and local wine — €11–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes and bring plenty of water for the caldera hike — the path can be uneven. Start early (8:00–9:00 AM) to avoid the midday heat. The hike is free and far more rewarding than any paid tour.

day_by_day.morning: Take the local bus to Akrotiri (€1.80) and visit the prehistoric Minoan settlement buried by the volcanic eruption — often called the 'Greek Pompeii.' Entry around €12. Fascinating and well-preserved ruins under a modern shelter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Red Beach (Kokkini Paralia) — one of Santorini's most dramatic and unique beaches with red volcanic cliffs. Free access (short rocky walk from the parking area). Swim and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fira by bus. Pack your bags for tomorrow's departure. Enjoy a final Santorini dinner and pick up some local products (cherry tomatoes, capers, local wine) as affordable souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or a tiropita and freddo cappuccino from a Fira bakery — €3–4
meals.lunch: Simple snack bar near Akrotiri or Red Beach — a sandwich and cold drink — €5–7
meals.dinner: Farewell Santorini dinner at a local taverna — moussaka, Greek salad, and a glass of Assyrtiko white wine — €12–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Red Beach can be slippery — wear water shoes if possible. Note that part of the path may be closed due to rockfall; check locally. Santorini's local Assyrtiko wine is world-class and affordable at local shops (€6–10 per bottle).

day_by_day.morning: Take an early ferry from Santorini to Crete (Heraklion port) — approximately 2 hours by high-speed ferry (~€35–45) or longer by conventional ferry (~€20–25). Book in advance. Arrive in Heraklion and check into a budget hostel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palace of Knossos (bus from Heraklion city center, ~€1.50 each way) — the legendary Minoan palace and one of Greece's most important archaeological sites. Entry around €15. Explore the reconstructed frescoes and labyrinthine ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Heraklion and stroll along the old Venetian harbor. Walk along the harbor walls to the Koules Fortress (entry €4). Enjoy the lively evening atmosphere in the city center.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack on the ferry or eat before departure in Santorini — a cheese pie — €2–3
meals.lunch: Taverna near Knossos — try Cretan dakos salad and a cold beer — €8–10
meals.dinner: Heraklion old town taverna — Cretan specialties like lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens) and local raki — €11–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Crete has a distinct culinary tradition — look for Cretan olive oil, thyme honey, and graviera cheese. Raki (tsikoudia) is often offered free at the end of a meal in Cretan tavernas — a lovely local custom.

day_by_day.morning: Take a KTEL bus from Heraklion to Matala (approximately 1.5 hours, ~€7 each way) — a legendary beach village famous for its ancient Roman cave dwellings carved into the cliffs. Explore the caves (small entry fee ~€3) and the beautiful sandy beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon swimming at Matala Beach or walk 20 minutes over the headland to Red Beach (Kokkinos Ammos) — a quieter, stunning cove with red-tinged sand. Both beaches are free to access.
day_by_day.evening: Return by KTEL bus to Heraklion. Enjoy a final evening in Crete with a leisurely dinner in the Lion Square (Plateia Venizelou) area — the heart of Heraklion's social life.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or a Cretan bakery — a kalitsounia (sweet cheese pastry) and coffee — €3–4
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood or a simple mezze plate at a taverna in Matala village — €9–12
meals.dinner: Heraklion taverna near Lion Square — grilled lamb chops, horta (wild greens), and local wine — €12–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Matala was a famous hippie hangout in the 1960s and 70s — Joni Mitchell reportedly stayed here. The KTEL bus station in Heraklion is near the port. Check return bus times carefully as evening services may be limited.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Crete. Visit the Heraklion Archaeological Museum (one of the world's finest collections of Minoan art — entry ~€10) if you haven't already. Alternatively, browse the local market on 1866 Street for last-minute food souvenirs — olive oil, honey, herbs, and cheese.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Heraklion Airport (Nikos Kazantzakis) for your return flight. The airport is very close to the city center — a taxi costs ~€10–12 or take a local bus for €1.50. Allow plenty of time for check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Heraklion. Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, ancient history, and delicious Greek food — all on a budget!

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — a proper sit-down meal of eggs, local cheese, olives, and coffee at a café near the hostel — €6–8
meals.lunch: Light meal or snack at the airport or grab a final souvlaki wrap in the city before heading to the airport — €4–5
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tips: Use local buses everywhere (€1.50–2 per ride), eat at tavernas away from tourist hotspots, buy picnic supplies from supermarkets and local markets, and take advantage of free attractions like beaches, hiking trails, and scenic walks. Total daily budget target: €50–70 per person including accommodation, food, transport, and entry fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora)
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local food guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and shop for local spices and ingredients. This indoor-friendly tour is perfect for avoiding midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day – flight lands at 14:50, so morning is in transit. Rest and settle into accommodation after landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 to central Athens. Check into your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Koukaki neighborhood. Take a gentle orientation stroll around Monastiraki Square and the Flea Market to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric Plaka neighborhood, the oldest district in Athens. Explore the narrow cobblestone streets, browse local shops, and soak in the ambiance beneath the Acropolis lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap from a street kiosk near Monastiraki Square (€3–5) after settling in
meals.dinner: Taverna Monastiri or a similar traditional taverna in Plaka – try moussaka, tzatziki, and a glass of local wine (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light due to travel fatigue. Exchange some euros at the airport or use an ATM. Metro Line 3 from the airport to Monastiraki takes about 40 minutes and costs €9.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora): Join the guided food tour of the historic Varvakios Agora starting early in the cool morning hours. Explore stalls overflowing with fresh fish, meat, spices, olives, and local cheeses with a knowledgeable local guide. Sample traditional Greek products and learn about Athenian food culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Monastiraki Flea Market and then head to the Ancient Agora of Athens – the heart of ancient Athenian civic life. Explore the well-preserved Stoa of Attalos museum and the Temple of Hephaestus (€10 entry). Enjoy views of the Acropolis from below.
day_by_day.evening: Head up to the Thissio neighborhood for sunset drinks at a rooftop café with Acropolis views. Then explore the trendy Psiri district for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Included in the food tour or grab a bougatsa (custard pastry) and Greek coffee at a local bakery near the market (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Taste samples from the food tour, supplemented by a souvlaki plate at a local grill near the Agora (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mezedopoleio (meze restaurant) in Psiri – share small plates like grilled octopus, saganaki, and spanakopita (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The food tour typically starts at 9:00–10:00 AM – book in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Ancient Agora is a 10-minute walk from Varvakios Agora.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis of Athens early (open from 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket (€30) includes entry to multiple archaeological sites. The views over Athens are spectacular in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis Museum (€15) at the base of the hill – one of Europe's finest archaeological museums. Spend 2–3 hours exploring artifacts from the Acropolis including original Parthenon friezes. Afterward, relax at a café in the Koukaki neighborhood below.
day_by_day.evening: Take the funicular up Lycabettus Hill for panoramic sunset views over all of Athens and the Saronic Gulf. Descend and have dinner in the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts at a café near your hotel (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Acropolis Museum café with Acropolis views (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Traditional Greek restaurant in Kolonaki – try lamb kleftiko or fresh grilled sea bream (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the Acropolis by 8:00–8:30 AM to avoid peak crowds and heat. Bring water and sunscreen. The combined archaeological ticket is valid for 5 days and covers 7 sites.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Cape Sounion: Take an early KTEL bus from Pedion Areos (departing ~7:30 AM, €7 each way, 2-hour journey) to the dramatic Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff 60 meters above the Aegean Sea. Explore the ruins and enjoy breathtaking coastal views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at the beautiful beach directly below the temple at Sounion Beach or the nearby Legrena Beach. The water is crystal clear and the setting is stunning. Bring snorkeling gear if possible.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens by late afternoon/early evening. Have a relaxed dinner in the Koukaki or Neos Kosmos neighborhood – local and less touristy than Plaka.

meals.breakfast: Grab a tiropita (cheese pie) and coffee from a bakery before catching the bus (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a taverna near Sounion Beach – grilled fish, Greek salad, and local wine (€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Neighborhood taverna in Koukaki – try slow-cooked stifado (beef stew) or pastitsio (€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check KTEL bus schedules in advance. The last bus back to Athens is typically around 7:00–8:00 PM. Bring a towel, sunscreen, and swimwear. June weather at 23°C is perfect for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Santorini: Take the early morning ferry from Piraeus Port (Athens) to Santorini – a high-speed ferry takes about 5 hours (€45–65). Alternatively, a 45-minute flight is available. Arrive in Santorini and check into a mid-range hotel in Fira or Firostefani.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Fira, the island's capital. Walk along the caldera-edge path, visit the Archaeological Museum of Thera (€6), and browse the local shops and galleries. The views of the volcanic caldera are iconic.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take the cable car down to the old port (Skala) and back up. Watch the famous Santorini sunset from the caldera-view terrace in Fira or begin the walk toward Imerovigli.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at Piraeus port café before boarding (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Onboard ferry snack or quick bite upon arrival in Fira (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a caldera-view restaurant in Fira – try fresh tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters), fava dip, and local Assyrtiko white wine (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance, especially for June. The high-speed ferry (SeaJets or Hellenic Seaways) is recommended. Fira is the most central base for exploring the island.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the famous Fira to Oia trail (10 km, 3–4 hours) along the caldera rim. Pass through Firostefani and Imerovigli with stunning volcanic views. The morning is the best time to hike before the heat peaks. Arrive in the iconic white-washed village of Oia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Oia village – browse the boutique shops, visit the Nautical Museum (€3), and find a quiet spot to admire the blue-domed churches and caldera views. Take a refreshing swim at Ammoudi Bay (300 steps below Oia) in the crystal-clear Aegean.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Oia for the world-famous sunset – find a good viewing spot early as it gets crowded. The sunset from Oia's castle ruins is spectacular. Have dinner in Oia before returning to Fira by local bus (€1.80).

meals.breakfast: Greek breakfast at your hotel or a café in Fira before the hike – eggs, olives, local cheese, bread (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a taverna in Ammoudi Bay below Oia – grilled octopus and local catch (€20–28 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Oia at a mid-range restaurant – try lamb chops with local herbs and a carafe of Vinsanto dessert wine (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Start the hike by 8:00 AM to avoid peak heat. Bring plenty of water (2L minimum), sunscreen, and a hat. The trail is well-marked but has some uneven sections. Buses run frequently between Oia and Fira.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the prehistoric site of Akrotiri – a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age city buried by the volcanic eruption of 1627 BC (€12 entry). Often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean,' it offers fascinating insight into ancient Aegean civilization. Visit early before the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the famous Red Beach near Akrotiri – one of Santorini's most dramatic beaches with towering red volcanic cliffs. Swim and relax. Then visit the nearby White Beach and Mesa Pigadia Beach, accessible by water taxi from Red Beach (€5 round trip).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fira and enjoy a leisurely evening. Visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera (€6) if not already visited, then enjoy a caldera-view dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local bakery in Fira – fresh bread, honey, and Greek coffee (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Casual beach taverna near Red Beach – Greek salad, grilled sardines, and cold Mythos beer (€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Fira with caldera views – try seafood pasta with local Santorini cherry tomatoes (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Red Beach requires a short rocky walk from the parking area – wear sturdy sandals. The beach can be crowded by midday. Akrotiri is partially covered so it's manageable even in heat.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Mykonos: Take the morning ferry from Santorini to Mykonos (2–3 hours by high-speed ferry, €35–55). Check into a mid-range hotel in Mykonos Town (Chora) or nearby. Drop your bags and head out to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Mykonos Town (Chora) – wander through the iconic labyrinthine white-washed alleys, visit the famous windmills at Kato Mili, and stroll through Little Venice where colorful buildings hang over the sea. Visit the Archaeological Museum of Mykonos (€4).
day_by_day.evening: Experience the vibrant atmosphere of Little Venice at sunset with a cocktail at one of the waterfront bars. Explore the lively Matogianni Street for shopping and people-watching. Have dinner in Chora.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast on the ferry or at Santorini port (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch in Mykonos Town upon arrival – try a local gyros or a fresh salad at a harbor café (€10–15)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional Greek taverna in Chora – try fresh grilled fish, loukoumades (honey donuts) for dessert (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance. Mykonos Town can be very busy in June – book restaurants for dinner in advance. The town is best explored on foot as streets are too narrow for vehicles.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the sacred island of Delos (UNESCO World Heritage Site): Take the short boat from Mykonos Town harbor (€20 round trip, 30 minutes). Explore one of the most important archaeological sites in Greece – the birthplace of Apollo and Artemis. Visit the iconic Terrace of the Lions and the ancient theater.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos by early afternoon. Head to Platis Gialos Beach – one of the island's most organized and beautiful beaches with golden sand and clear water. Rent a sunbed (€8–12) and enjoy the afternoon swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the beach bars and sunset spots along the southern coast, then return to Mykonos Town for the famous nightlife. Enjoy dinner before the evening gets too late.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait and coffee at a café in Chora before the boat (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks on Delos (no restaurants on the island – bring water and food) or eat at Platis Gialos beach taverna upon return (€15–20)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mezedopoleio in Mykonos Town – share plates of grilled vegetables, kopanisti cheese spread, and fresh calamari (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Delos boats depart at 9:00 AM and 10:00 AM; last return is at 3:00 PM. Bring water, sunscreen, and a hat – there is no shade on Delos. The site is extensive; allow 2–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ano Mera village in the interior of Mykonos – a refreshingly authentic and non-touristy village. Visit the 16th-century Panagia Tourliani Monastery (free entry) with its ornate marble fountain. Browse the local market and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere away from the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Elia Beach – Mykonos's longest beach on the southeastern coast, known for its beautiful clear water and more relaxed atmosphere than the party beaches. Swim, snorkel, and relax. Water sports are available for rent.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for a final evening. Visit the Folklore Museum (free) near the harbor, then enjoy a sunset cocktail at a Little Venice bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Traditional breakfast at a café in Ano Mera village – fresh bread, local honey, and strong Greek coffee (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beach taverna at Elia Beach – grilled sea bass, Greek salad, and fresh lemonade (€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Farewell Mykonos dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Chora – try lamb souvlaki with pita and a bottle of local Cycladic wine (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Buses run from Mykonos Town to Ano Mera and Elia Beach. Alternatively, rent an ATV (€25–35/day) to explore the island independently – a popular and fun option.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day back to Athens: Take the morning ferry or flight from Mykonos to Athens (ferry ~5 hours or 45-minute flight). Check back into your Athens hotel or a new one near the airport if departing soon. If time allows, visit the National Archaeological Museum (€12) – the world's finest collection of ancient Greek artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Exarchia neighborhood – Athens's bohemian, intellectual quarter with independent bookshops, street art, and authentic local cafés. Visit the Epigraphical Museum (free) or simply enjoy the neighborhood's unique character. Browse the street market if it's running.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Gazi neighborhood for Athens's best food and nightlife scene. Visit the Technopolis cultural complex (former gasworks, now an arts venue). Enjoy a final Athens evening with dinner at one of Gazi's excellent restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Mykonos port café before boarding (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Exarchia at a local taverna – try the daily special (mageirefta) for an authentic and affordable meal (€10–15 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Gazi – try a modern Greek restaurant with creative takes on traditional dishes; grilled lamb chops with kritharoto (orzo risotto) (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book return transport in advance. If flying back to Athens, the journey is much faster. The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Tuesdays – check opening hours.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Benaki Museum (€9) – one of Greece's most important private museums covering Greek history from prehistoric times to the 20th century, housed in a beautiful neoclassical mansion. Excellent collection of Byzantine art, traditional costumes, and Greek War of Independence artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Athens Riviera: Take the tram from Syntagma Square to Glyfada (30 minutes, €1.40) – Athens's coastal suburb with a beautiful waterfront promenade, marina, and excellent beaches. Swim at Asteras Beach or Vouliagmeni Beach (€8–15 entry for organized beaches). The water is warm and clear.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Athens for a final evening. Visit the Syntagma Square to watch the Evzone guards at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Enjoy a farewell dinner in the Psiri or Monastiraki area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a traditional kafeneion (Greek coffee house) near your hotel – Greek coffee, koulouri (sesame bread ring), and tiropita (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a seafood restaurant along the Glyfada waterfront – fresh grilled fish and a cold Assyrtiko wine (€20–28 per person)
meals.dinner: Final Athens dinner at a rooftop restaurant with Acropolis views in Monastiraki – try the chef's tasting menu of Greek classics (€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Vouliagmeni (thermal lake) is also nearby and worth a visit (€8 entry) – the warm mineral waters are said to have healing properties. The tram to Glyfada runs frequently from Syntagma.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens: Visit the Kerameikos Archaeological Site (€8) – the ancient cemetery of Athens, less crowded than other sites but historically fascinating. Walk through the ancient burial grounds and visit the excellent on-site museum. Afterward, browse the nearby Monastiraki Flea Market for last-minute souvenirs – local honey, olive oil, herbs, and ceramics make great gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final Greek lunch in Athens. Visit any remaining sites or simply relax at a café in Thissio with Acropolis views. Pack and prepare for departure. Head to Athens International Airport via Metro Line 3 from Monastiraki (40 minutes, €9).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Athens International Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of Greek beaches, ancient history, and incredible food.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at a neighborhood café – fresh orange juice, Greek yogurt with thyme honey, and a freddo espresso (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a traditional taverna in Thissio – try the classic Greek salad, tzatziki, grilled octopus, and a final glass of ouzo (€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Light meal at the airport or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the Metro journey and airport check-in. Purchase any duty-free Greek products (olive oil, wine, honey) at the airport. Keep some euros for the Metro ticket and any last-minute purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Sunset Sailing & Snorkeling Around Santorini Caldera
experiences.description: Join a small-group catamaran cruise departing in the late afternoon around the volcanic caldera of Santorini. Snorkel in crystal-clear Aegean waters, visit the Red and White beaches, and enjoy a traditional Greek mezze spread with local wine on board as you watch the legendary Oia sunset from the sea.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora)
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local food guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and shop for local spices and ingredients. This indoor-friendly tour is perfect for avoiding midday heat.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Morning Visit
experiences.description: Arrive early at the stunning Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete to enjoy its famous pink-tinged sand and shallow turquoise lagoons before the midday crowds and heat arrive. Wade across the shallow sandbar to the small island, collect sea glass, and swim in calm, warm waters. Pack a local picnic from a nearby bakery for a perfect morning escape.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in a Cretan Village
experiences.description: Spend a morning in a family-run kitchen in a traditional Cretan village learning to prepare authentic dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and galaktoboureko (custard pastry). The class takes place indoors making it an ideal midday heat or rain alternative. Enjoy the meal you prepare with local raki and wine.

experiences.name: Evening Taverna Crawl in Nafplio Old Town
experiences.description: As temperatures cool in the evening, stroll through the charming Venetian old town of Nafplio and hop between traditional tavernas sampling local Peloponnesian specialties: grilled octopus, tomatokeftedes, fresh grilled fish, and local Nemea red wine. The cobblestone streets and neoclassical architecture create a magical atmosphere perfect for a leisurely evening of authentic Greek dining and culture.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 on Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your hotel in central Athens. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around Syntagma Square and the National Garden to begin soaking in the Athenian atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle orientation walk through the Plaka neighborhood — the oldest district of Athens — admiring the neoclassical architecture and the illuminated Acropolis above. Enjoy a welcome dinner at a rooftop restaurant with Acropolis views.

meals.breakfast: Meal on board or at the airport
meals.lunch: Light snack at Athens Airport arrivals lounge or airport premium café
meals.dinner: Dinner at Strofi Restaurant (Rovertou Galli 25, Makrigianni) — a classic Athenian taverna with legendary Acropolis views; try the lamb chops, grilled octopus, and local Assyrtiko white wine

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. Keep Day 1 light given travel fatigue. Athens weather in June is warm (~23°C) and mostly dry — perfect for evening walks.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Acropolis and Parthenon (open from 08:00) before the crowds and midday heat arrive. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance. Follow with a visit to the Acropolis Museum, one of the finest archaeological museums in the world, housing original Parthenon sculptures and artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora) — explore the vibrant historic market with a local food guide, tasting cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, spices, and street food. Afterward, wander through Monastiraki flea market and browse artisan shops in the Psyrri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktails at a rooftop bar in Monastiraki with Acropolis views, followed by a refined dinner in Kolonaki, Athens' most upscale neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at a traditional Athenian café — Greek yogurt with thyme honey, spanakopita, and freddo espresso
meals.lunch: Tasting bites during the Varvakios Agora food tour; supplement with a mezze spread at a traditional ouzeri in the market area
meals.dinner: Dinner at Spondi (Pyrronos 5, Pangrati) — Athens' most celebrated fine-dining restaurant with two Michelin stars; Mediterranean tasting menu with exceptional Greek wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets and the Varvakios food tour well in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sun protection. The food tour typically lasts 3–4 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ancient Agora of Athens and the remarkably preserved Temple of Hephaestus. Continue to the Roman Agora and the Tower of the Winds. Explore the Anafiotika quarter — a tiny Cycladic-style village hidden within the Plaka, with whitewashed houses and bougainvillea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the National Archaeological Museum, home to the world's finest collection of ancient Greek antiquities including the Antikythera Mechanism and the Mask of Agamemnon. Afterward, relax with a coffee in the upscale Kolonaki district.
day_by_day.evening: Evening at leisure in Athens. Enjoy a sunset aperitivo at a rooftop bar, then dinner at a celebrated modern Greek restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or brunch at Couleur Locale (Normanou 3, Monastiraki) — stunning rooftop café with Acropolis views and excellent coffee and pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tzitzikas & Mermingas (Mitropoleos 12, Syntagma) — beloved modern taverna serving creative takes on Greek classics in a lively setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nolan (Voulis 11, Syntagma) — innovative Greek-Asian fusion by acclaimed chef Sotiris Kontizas; outstanding tasting menu with natural Greek wines

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is best visited in the afternoon when morning crowds thin. Consider hiring a private guide for a richer experience. Comfortable shoes essential.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens by private transfer or domestic flight to Nafplio in the Peloponnese (approximately 2.5 hours by car or arrange a scenic drive via the coastal road). Check into your luxury boutique hotel in Nafplio Old Town. Take a morning walk along the waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the magnificent Palamidi Fortress — climb the 999 steps (or take a taxi to the top) for panoramic views over the Argolic Gulf and the old town. Visit the Bourtzi Castle, a small Venetian fortress on an islet in the harbor, accessible by short boat ride.
day_by_day.evening: Evening Taverna Crawl in Nafplio Old Town — stroll through the charming Venetian lanes, stopping at traditional tavernas for small plates: grilled saganaki, stuffed vine leaves, local Nemea red wine, and fresh seafood mezze. End the evening with a dessert of loukoumades (honey doughnuts) at a traditional sweet shop.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel or a café in Syntagma Square, Athens, before departure
meals.lunch: Light lunch upon arrival in Nafplio at a waterfront café — fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and local bread
meals.dinner: Taverna crawl through Nafplio Old Town — recommended stops include Aiolos Taverna and To Omorfo Tavernaki for authentic Peloponnesian cuisine and local Nemea wines

day_by_day.notes: Nafplio is considered one of Greece's most romantic and beautiful towns. Book a boutique hotel within the old town walls for the best experience (e.g., Nafplia Palace or Amymone). The Palamidi climb is strenuous — start in the cooler late afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the ancient site of Mycenae (45 minutes from Nafplio) — explore the legendary Bronze Age citadel, the Lion Gate, the Treasury of Atreus (Tomb of Agamemnon), and the Archaeological Museum of Mycenae. This UNESCO World Heritage Site is one of Greece's most important ancient ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ancient theater of Epidaurus (30 minutes from Mycenae) — one of the best-preserved ancient Greek theaters, famous for its extraordinary acoustics. Return to Nafplio for a relaxing afternoon swim at Arvanitia Beach, a small rocky cove just below the old town walls.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on a terrace overlooking the Argolic Gulf, followed by a refined dinner at one of Nafplio's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Greek yogurt, local honey, fresh fruit, pastries, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near Epidaurus or a taverna lunch in the village of Ligourio near the theater — grilled meats, horiatiki salad, and local wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Arapakos Restaurant (Bouboulinas 81, Nafplio) — renowned for the freshest seafood on the waterfront; try the grilled sea bream, lobster pasta, and local Moschofilero white wine

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private guide for Mycenae and Epidaurus for a much richer historical experience. Bring water and sun protection. Check if any evening performances are scheduled at the Epidaurus theater during your visit — attending a classical drama there is a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Nafplio by private transfer to Athens Airport (approximately 2.5 hours). Fly to Heraklion, Crete (approximately 1-hour flight). Transfer to your luxury resort on the northern coast of Crete (Elounda or Agios Nikolaos area). Check in and settle into your villa or suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and decompress at your resort — enjoy the private pool, beach, or spa. Take a gentle walk along the Cretan coastline and explore the immediate surroundings. Optional: visit the charming harbor town of Agios Nikolaos for a coffee and a stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at your resort's signature restaurant, or dine at a waterfront taverna in Elounda overlooking the tranquil bay.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at hotel before departure or at Athens Airport
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Heraklion Airport or upon arrival at the resort
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ferryman Taverna (Elounda waterfront) — iconic Cretan seafood restaurant with exceptional fresh fish, Cretan dakos salad, and local Vidiano white wine; stunning sunset views over the bay

day_by_day.notes: Elounda is home to some of Greece's most exclusive resorts (e.g., Blue Palace Elounda, Domes of Elounda). Book well in advance. The drive from Heraklion to Elounda takes approximately 1 hour along a scenic coastal road.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in a Cretan Village — spend the morning in a family-run kitchen in a traditional village in the Cretan countryside. Learn to prepare authentic dishes: dakos, spanakopita, lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and loukoumades. Enjoy the meal you've prepared together.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palace of Knossos (near Heraklion) — the legendary Minoan palace complex, one of Europe's oldest cities and the mythological home of the Minotaur's labyrinth. Explore with a private guide for the full historical context. Afterward, visit the Heraklion Archaeological Museum, which houses the world's finest Minoan collection.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Elounda for a relaxing evening. Sunset drinks at your resort's infinity pool bar, followed by a leisurely dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before the cooking class
meals.lunch: The dishes prepared during the cooking class — a full traditional Cretan feast
meals.dinner: Dinner at Elia Restaurant at your resort or at Pouliezos (Elounda) — excellent Cretan cuisine with a modern twist, featuring local cheeses, slow-cooked lamb, and Cretan wines

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically runs 3–4 hours including the meal. Book in advance. Knossos is best visited in the afternoon when morning tour groups depart. A private guide at Knossos is highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Elafonissi Beach Morning Visit — depart early (around 07:00) for the 2.5-hour drive to Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete. Arrive before the crowds to enjoy the famous pink-tinged sand, crystal-clear turquoise lagoon, and shallow warm waters. Swim, snorkel, and relax in one of the Mediterranean's most beautiful natural settings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the southwestern coast — visit the dramatic Kedrodasos Beach (a short walk from Elafonissi, known for its cedar forest) or drive to the scenic village of Paleochora for lunch. Begin the return drive to Elounda, stopping at the Venetian fortress of Frangokastello along the south coast.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at the resort by early evening. Enjoy a spa treatment to recover from the day's travel, followed by a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — pack snacks and water for the journey
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a taverna in Paleochora harbor — grilled octopus, fried calamari, and local Cretan salad with graviera cheese
meals.dinner: Dinner at your resort's fine-dining restaurant — indulge in a full Cretan tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The round trip to Elafonissi is approximately 5 hours of driving — consider hiring a private driver for comfort. Bring snorkeling gear, reef shoes, sunscreen, and plenty of water. Arrive by 08:00 to secure a good spot before the beach fills up.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Crete by domestic flight from Heraklion to Santorini (approximately 45 minutes). Transfer to your luxury caldera-view hotel in Oia or Imerovigli. Check in and take in the breathtaking views of the volcanic caldera, the deep blue Aegean, and the iconic white-and-blue architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Oia village on foot — wander through the narrow cobblestone lanes, browse high-end art galleries and jewelry boutiques, and discover hidden viewpoints over the caldera. Visit the Byzantine Castle ruins at the northern tip of Oia for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Sailing & Snorkeling Around Santorini Caldera — join a small-group luxury catamaran cruise departing in the late afternoon. Sail around the volcanic caldera, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters near the hot springs, and watch the legendary Santorini sunset from the water with champagne and a light dinner on board.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Elounda resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a caldera-view restaurant in Oia upon arrival — try Ammoudi Fish Tavern (Ammoudi Bay, below Oia) for the freshest grilled fish and seafood, reached by a scenic staircase descent
meals.dinner: Light dinner and drinks served on board the catamaran cruise — fresh salads, grilled meats, local cheeses, and Santorini Assyrtiko wine as the sun sets over the caldera

day_by_day.notes: Book your caldera-view hotel well in advance — top choices include Canaves Oia Epitome, Grace Santorini, or Mystique. The catamaran sunset cruise is one of Santorini's signature experiences — book a premium small-group tour (max 10–12 guests) for the best experience. Oia's famous sunset draws large crowds at the castle — the catamaran offers a far superior vantage point.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age city buried by the volcanic eruption of 1627 BC, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' Explore with a private guide. Afterward, visit the Red Beach (Kokkini Paralia) nearby — one of Santorini's most dramatic volcanic beaches with towering red and black cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Perissa or Perivolos Beach on the southeastern coast — Santorini's longest black volcanic sand beach. Rent a premium sunbed at a beach club, swim in the clear Aegean, and enjoy the unique experience of black sand beaches. Optional: rent a quad bike or ATV to explore the island's volcanic landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Oia or Fira for the evening. Enjoy cocktails at a caldera-view bar, then a refined dinner at one of Santorini's celebrated restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel — most caldera hotels offer exceptional breakfast with views; enjoy Greek yogurt, local honey, fresh fruit, and eggs with a glass of fresh orange juice
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch at Perivolos Beach — fresh seafood, salads, and chilled Santorini wine at a premium beach club such as Wet Stories or Seaside
meals.dinner: Dinner at Selene Restaurant (Pyrgos village) — Santorini's most acclaimed fine-dining restaurant, celebrating local Santorinian ingredients; exceptional tasting menu with volcanic island wines

day_by_day.notes: Akrotiri requires advance ticket booking. The Red Beach involves a short rocky walk — wear sturdy sandals. Perivolos Beach clubs offer full-day sunbed and umbrella service with food and drink menus.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast at your hotel with caldera views. Take a private yoga or meditation session on your hotel terrace if available. Explore the village of Pyrgos — Santorini's highest village, with a Venetian castle, traditional architecture, and sweeping 360-degree island views. Visit a local winery for a morning wine tasting of Santorini's unique Assyrtiko and Vinsanto wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Fira, Santorini's capital — explore the Museum of Prehistoric Thera (housing Akrotiri artifacts), the Orthodox Metropolitan Cathedral, and the Catholic Cathedral. Walk the famous caldera path from Fira to Imerovigli (approximately 3 km, 1.5 hours) for spectacular views. Relax at your hotel pool in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Santorini — dress up for a special sunset dinner at a premium caldera-view restaurant in Oia.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast with caldera views — the highlight of any Santorini morning
meals.lunch: Wine tasting lunch at Santo Wines Winery (Pyrgos) — the island's most scenic winery with a terrace overlooking the caldera; mezze platters paired with Assyrtiko, Nykteri, and Vinsanto wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lauda Restaurant at Mystique Hotel (Oia) — one of Santorini's most exclusive dining experiences with dramatic caldera views, creative Mediterranean cuisine, and an exceptional Greek wine list

day_by_day.notes: The Fira-to-Imerovigli caldera walk is moderately easy but involves some steps — wear comfortable shoes. Book the Lauda dinner reservation well in advance as it is one of the most sought-after tables on the island.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Santorini — wake up early for one last sunrise over the caldera (Santorini's sunrises are as spectacular as the sunsets, with far fewer crowds). Enjoy a long, leisurely breakfast at your hotel. Pack and check out. Transfer to Santorini Airport for a domestic flight back to Athens (approximately 45 minutes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Athens and transfer to a luxury hotel near the city center for your final night. Revisit any favorite spots — perhaps a final walk through Plaka, a visit to a gallery in Kolonaki, or a relaxing afternoon at a rooftop pool. Optional: visit the Benaki Museum for an outstanding collection of Greek art spanning 5,000 years.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Athens — celebrate the end of a magnificent Greek journey at one of the city's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast in Santorini with caldera views — make it special
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Athens upon arrival — mezze and wine at a stylish restaurant in Kolonaki or Psyrri
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Varoulko Seaside (Akti Koumoundourou 52, Piraeus) — Michelin-starred seafood restaurant by legendary chef Lefteris Lazarou; extraordinary creative Greek seafood cuisine with premium wine pairings; a truly memorable final dinner

day_by_day.notes: Varoulko Seaside is located in Piraeus (20 minutes from central Athens) — arrange a private transfer. Book well in advance. This is widely considered one of the best restaurants in Greece and a perfect way to conclude a luxury Greek journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Depending on your departure flight time, take a final stroll through the city: visit the Zappeion Gardens, walk along the Panathenaic Stadium (site of the first modern Olympic Games in 1896), or browse high-end boutiques on Voukourestiou Street for last-minute gifts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Athens International Airport for your return flight. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days exploring the beaches, ancient history, and incredible food of Greece.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry home memories of Santorini sunsets, Cretan cooking, Athenian ruins, and the warm hospitality of the Greek people.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast in Athens — enjoy Greek yogurt, honey, pastries, and strong Greek coffee one last time
meals.lunch: Lunch at the airport or a final quick meal near the hotel before transfer — try a traditional souvlaki wrap from a premium street food spot as a last taste of Greece
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Athens Airport has good shopping and dining options if you have time before your flight. Consider purchasing local products as gifts: Santorini Assyrtiko wine, Cretan extra-virgin olive oil, thyme honey, mastiha liqueur from Chios, or handmade jewelry from Oia. Confirm your return flight details and arrange airport transfer the evening before.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC
